claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children.

Let me start with a few basic questions:

**What are the names and ages of the children you're inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex, who's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 17 years old.

To continue assessing eligibility, I need to ask:

**Are you the parent or guardian responsible for Alex, and are you living in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm Alex's parent and I live in the UK. Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. That's helpful information.

Now I need to ask about Alex's current situation:

**Is Alex in full-time education or training, or does Alex have any other status I should know about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex recently started an apprenticeship, actually. He's training in a trade.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know that Alex is doing an apprenticeship in a trade.

To help determine eligibility, I need a bit more detail:

**Is Alex's apprenticeship a full-time apprenticeship, and approximately how much does Alex earn per week from the apprenticeship?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's a full-time apprenticeship. I'm not entirely sure about the exact weekly earnings - is that important for the Child Benefit eligibility?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's a good question. Let me clarify: the amount Alex earns from the apprenticeship isn't what matters for Child Benefit eligibility. What's more relevant is whether Alex is in approved education or training.

Let me ask this instead:

**When did Alex start the apprenticeship, and do you know if it's a recognized apprenticeship programme (for example, through a training provider or employer)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He started it fairly recently - just a few months ago. Yes, it's a proper recognized apprenticeship through his employer and a training provider. Is that the kind of thing that counts for Child Benefit purposes?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, that's the right kind of information. A recognized apprenticeship through an employer and training provider is relevant to Child Benefit eligibility.

Now, I have one more important question:

**Has Alex finished or left any full-time education (such as secondary school or college) before starting this apprenticeship, or did he go straight into the apprenticeship?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He left school before starting the apprenticeship - he finished his GCSEs and then went straight into this apprenticeship programme.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. That's very helpful.

I just need to confirm one final detail:

**Is Alex still under 19 years old, or has he already turned 19?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's 17, so yes, he's still under 19.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for confirming all of that information. I now have everything I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review the situation:
- Alex is 17 years old
- Alex is your child and lives with you in the UK
- Alex is in a full-time recognized apprenticeship through an employer and training provider
- Alex started the apprenticeship a few months ago after finishing GCSEs
- Alex is under 19 years old

Based on the Child Benefit eligibility rules, young people in approved apprenticeships are eligible for Child Benefit continuation until they reach 19, provided they remain in that approved training. Since Alex meets all these criteria, you should be eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent news! **You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Alex qualifies because:
- He is under 19 years old
- He is in a full-time recognized apprenticeship, which is an approved form of training
- He lives with you in the UK

Child Benefit can continue for young people in approved apprenticeships until they turn 19. As long as Alex remains in this apprenticeship, you should be able to claim Child Benefit for him.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
